newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cocoa consumers stick to low price targets.
newsitem.headline: German cocoa consumers stick to low price targets.

text.p: German cocoa processors have no plans to revise their buying targets for beans and butter, which are 0.15-0.20 marks per kilo below the price range on offer, traders said.

Futures were viewed as too high against the background of fundamentals information while sterling's historic strength versus the mark also choked off demand -- despite the currency's four-pfennig dive on Wednesday.
"Consumers may not come back into the market this month until their price ideas are being met," one trader said.
"Alternatively, we would need fresh news on Ivorian crops to move the market either way."
An El Nino weather pattern could bring dry weather to West Africa and could negatively affect the 1997/98 mid crop, crop experts have said, but this could be offset by generally higher output.
Cash buyers here were also sidelined because a number of plants were shut down for annual maintenance during the holiday season.
Aug/Sept 1997 beans of good West African quality were offered at 3.04 marks cif, up five pfennigs on the week.
Fourth quarter beans were at 3.11 marks and first quarter 1998 at 3.09.
Nearby cocoa butter was at 7.60 marks per kilo liquid, ex-works, with the fourth quarter was at 7.70 and first quarter at 7.75.
Sterling was at 3.0097 marks at the daily Frankfurt exchange fixing versus 2.9915 marks last week. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
